newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Seat to invest 120 bln pta in 4 years.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Seat to invest 120 bln pta in 4 years.

text.p: Volkswagen's Spanish unit Seat will invest around 120 billion pesetas in the next four years, new chairman Pierre-Alain de Smedt said on Tuesday.
He added that Seat intends to launch between three and five new models before 2000.
"This means we have to invest around 30 billion pesetas each year. So, in four years we will reach 120 billion in investments," he told regional newspaper La Vanguardia.
Full 1996 results for once financially troubled Seat will be announced on March 25, but the company's managers reiterated in different occasions that the carmaker is now on a positive trend.
They said 1996 was positive thanks to money transfers from the parent company, while Seat is expected to end 1997 with a profit without any outside help.
Seat lost 11.29 billion pesetas in 1995, after a loss of around 29.47 billion pesetas in 1994, and record negative value of 151.31 billion pesetas in 1993.
